div.head: Ps Cn for 25
div.ab: Si uero occiderit, amittat liberalis scutum liberalitatis; si sit illiberalis, careat libertate, si seruus uita.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 624 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: But if he kills it, let the noble lose the shield of his nobility; if he is a non-noble, let him lose his freedom; if a slave, his life.

note.seg: Bei hier zitiertem Math. Paris heisst libertas ‘Privileg der Immunität und Exemtion’, nicht Adelstand. — Ritter (s. d. Gl 6. a) Osbert Giffard ward 1285 im Geistlichen Gerichte Canterburys verurteilt: insigniis militaribus sit privatus; Selden Tituli honor. II 5, 38. Über scutum gentilitium und die Strafe der Entziehung der Waffen, u. a. des scutum gegen Gefolgsleute in Frankreich, s. E. Mayer Frz. Dt. Vfg. II 134. 163. — Zu libertate carere s. o. 15a

In Matthew Paris, quoted here, libertas means ‘privilege of immunity and exemption’, not noble rank. — The knight (see that word in Gl 6. a) Osbert Giffard was sentenced in 1285 in the ecclesiastical court of Canterbury: insigniis militaribus sit privatus; Selden Tituli honor. II 5, 38. On the scutum gentilitium and the penalty of taking away arms, among them the scutum, from vassals in France, see E. Mayer Frz. Dt. Vfg. II 134. 163. — On libertate carere see above 15a
